title: Commonly Confused Words & Spelling
why: The 2022 IPO paper had a full block of five "fill the right word" questions built on confusable sets (indigenous/ingenious/ingenuous, complement/compliment, edition/addition, accept/except, affect/effect). They are quick marks if you know the pairs and easy to lose if you rely on sound. Spelling questions ("choose the correctly spelt word") are standard in MPSC-type papers and are won with a handful of rules and a list of repeat offenders.

lessons.title: How to beat confusable-word questions
lessons.body:
Confusable words sound or look alike but differ in meaning or in **part of speech**. The examiner writes a sentence with a blank and gives you the whole family as options.

### Three checks, in order

1. **Part-of-speech check.** What does the blank need: a noun, a verb, an adjective? *"I need your ___"* needs a noun, so **advice**; *"I ___ you to rest"* needs a verb, so **advise**. This alone solves about half of these questions.
2. **Meaning check.** If two options are the same part of speech (eminent / imminent), use the meaning tables in the next lessons.
3. **Mnemonic check.** Attach one hook to each pair, e.g. station**e**ry = **e**nvelopes; stationary = st**a**nding still.

### Pattern families worth noticing

| Pattern | Noun | Verb | Hook |
|---|---|---|---|
| -ice / -ise | advice, practice, licence, device | advise, practise, license, devise | noun has **c** like "**c**oncrete thing"; verb has **s** |
| -th / -the | breath, bath, cloth | breathe, bathe, clothe | the verb takes the extra **e** |
| affect / effect | effect (result) | affect (influence) | **A**ffect = **A**ction (verb), **E**ffect = **E**nd result (noun) |

> In British/Indian usage, *practice* and *licence* are nouns, *practise* and *license* verbs. American English uses *practice* and *license* for both, so Indian exams follow the British rule.

lessons.title: Grammar-function confusables
lessons.body:
These differ mainly in their grammatical job. Learn the example sentence, not just the meaning.

| Words | Meaning / job | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Accept** / **Except** | receive, agree / leaving out | She accepted the gift. Everyone came except Ravi. |
| **Affect** / **Effect** | to influence (verb) / result (noun); *effect* as verb = bring about | Smoking affects health. Its effect is serious. The new chief effected many reforms. |
| **Advice** / **Advise** | suggestion (noun) / to suggest (verb) | Take my advice. I advise you to rest. |
| **Practice** / **Practise** | noun / verb (British) | Practice makes perfect. Practise daily. |
| **Device** / **Devise** | gadget (noun) / to plan (verb) | A new device. They devised a plan. |
| **Breath** / **Breathe** | noun / verb | Take a deep breath. Breathe slowly. |
| **Envelope** / **Envelop** | paper cover (noun) / to wrap (verb) | Seal the envelope. Fog enveloped Shillong. |
| **Loath** / **Loathe** | unwilling (adjective) / to hate (verb) | He was loath to leave. I loathe lies. |
| **Its** / **It's** | belonging to it / it is | The dog wagged its tail. It's raining. |
| **Their** / **There** / **They're** | belonging to them / that place / they are | Their house is there; they're at home. |
| **Whose** / **Who's** | of whom / who is | Whose pen is this? Who's calling? |
| **Your** / **You're** | belonging to you / you are | Your book. You're late. |
| **Lose** / **Loose** | to misplace, fail to win / not tight | Don't lose the key. A loose shirt. |
| **Lie** / **Lay** | recline (lie-lay-lain) / put down (lay-laid-laid) | I lie down. Lay the book on the table. |
| **Than** / **Then** | comparison / time | Taller than me. First eat, then sleep. |
| **Fewer** / **Less** | countable / uncountable | Fewer mistakes; less water. |
| **Farther** / **Further** | physical distance / additional, more (*further* is also accepted for distance in modern usage; exams usually expect *farther*) | Shillong is farther than Guwahati. No further questions. |
| **Beside** / **Besides** | next to / in addition to | Sit beside me. Besides English, he speaks Khasi. |
| **Later** / **Latter** | afterwards / second of two | See you later. Of tea and coffee, I prefer the latter. |
| **Lead** / **Led** | to guide (present); a metal / past of lead | Lead the team. She led the team yesterday. |
| **Formally** / **Formerly** | in a formal way / earlier, previously | Dress formally. He was formerly a teacher. |
| **Born** / **Borne** | given birth / carried, endured | He was born in Tura. Costs will be borne by the state. |
| **Hanged** / **Hung** | executed by hanging / suspended (objects) | The murderer was hanged. The picture was hung. |
| **Quiet** / **Quite** / **Quit** | silent / fairly, completely / leave | Be quiet. Quite good. He quit the job. |
| **Allowed** / **Aloud** | permitted / audibly | Phones are not allowed. Read aloud. |

lessons.title: Meaning confusables (look-alike words)
lessons.body:
Same part of speech, different meaning. These are the "choose the appropriate word" favourites.

| Words | Meanings | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Adapt** / **Adopt** / **Adept** | adjust / take up as one's own / skilled | Adapt to the climate. Adopt a child. Adept at chess. |
| **Allusion** / **Illusion** / **Delusion** | indirect reference / false appearance / false belief held firmly | An allusion to Tagore. An optical illusion. Delusions of grandeur. |
| **Credible** / **Creditable** / **Credulous** | believable / praiseworthy / too ready to believe | A credible witness. A creditable result. A credulous villager. |
| **Eminent** / **Imminent** / **Immanent** | famous / about to happen / present within | An eminent scientist. The storm is imminent. God is immanent in nature. |
| **Ingenious** / **Ingenuous** / **Indigenous** | clever, inventive / innocent, naive / native | An ingenious device. An ingenuous child. Indigenous tribes. |
| **Discreet** / **Discrete** | careful, tactful / separate, distinct | Be discreet. Discrete parts. |
| **Elicit** / **Illicit** | draw out / illegal | Elicit a reply. Illicit liquor. |
| **Eligible** / **Legible** | qualified / readable | Eligible for the post. Legible writing. |
| **Emigrate** / **Immigrate** | leave one's country / enter a new country | Emigrate from India; immigrate to Canada. |
| **Economic** / **Economical** | related to the economy / thrifty, not wasteful | Economic policy. An economical car. |
| **Historic** / **Historical** | important in history / related to history | A historic victory. A historical novel. |
| **Continual** / **Continuous** | repeated, with breaks / without any break | Continual interruptions. Continuous rain for six hours. |
| **Conscious** / **Conscience** | aware / inner moral sense | Conscious of the danger. A clear conscience. |
| **Official** / **Officious** | authorised / too eager to give orders | An official letter. An officious clerk. |
| **Judicial** / **Judicious** | of courts / wise, sensible | Judicial review. A judicious choice. |
| **Respectful** / **Respectable** / **Respective** | showing respect / deserving respect / belonging to each | Respectful to elders. A respectable family. Went to their respective homes. |
| **Sensible** / **Sensitive** | practical / easily affected | A sensible decision. Sensitive skin. |
| **Industrial** / **Industrious** | of industry / hard-working | An industrial area. An industrious student. |
| **Human** / **Humane** | of people / kind, compassionate | Human error. Humane treatment. |
| **Ensure** / **Insure** / **Assure** | make certain / buy insurance / promise, remove doubt | Ensure safety. Insure the car. I assure you. |
| **Imply** / **Infer** | suggest (speaker) / conclude (listener) | He implied I was lazy. I inferred he was angry. |
| **Proceed** / **Precede** | go ahead / come before | Proceed to gate 4. Lightning precedes thunder. |
| **Prescribe** / **Proscribe** | recommend (medicine, rule) / ban | Prescribe rest. The group was proscribed. |
| **Persecute** / **Prosecute** | harass, oppress / take legal action | Persecuted for his faith. Prosecuted for fraud. |
| **Adverse** / **Averse** | unfavourable / unwilling, opposed | Adverse weather. Averse to hard work. |
| **Amiable** / **Amicable** | friendly (person) / friendly (agreement, relation) | An amiable host. An amicable settlement. |
| **Uninterested** / **Disinterested** | not interested / impartial | Uninterested in cricket. A disinterested judge. |
| **Complacent** / **Complaisant** | self-satisfied / eager to please | Don't grow complacent. A complaisant host. |
| **Deprecate** / **Depreciate** | disapprove of / fall in value | He deprecated violence. The rupee depreciated. |
| **Momentary** / **Momentous** | lasting a moment / very important | A momentary pause. A momentous decision. |
| **Popular** / **Populous** | liked by many / having many people | A popular singer. A populous state. |
| **Childish** / **Childlike** | silly (negative) / innocent (positive) | Childish behaviour. Childlike wonder. |
| **Exceptional** / **Exceptionable** | outstanding, unusual / objectionable | Exceptional talent. Exceptionable language. |
| **Beneficial** / **Beneficent** | useful, helpful / doing good, kind | Beneficial exercise. A beneficent ruler. |
| **Urban** / **Urbane** | of a city / polished, courteous | Urban areas. An urbane diplomat. |
| **Veracity** / **Voracity** | truthfulness / greediness | Doubt his veracity. Ate with voracity. |
| **Elusive** / **Illusive** | hard to catch / deceptive, unreal | An elusive thief. An illusive hope. |
| **Access** / **Excess** | entry, approach / too much | Access to the files. An excess of sugar. |
| **Accede** / **Exceed** | agree to / go beyond | Accede to a request. Exceed the limit. |
| **Edition** / **Addition** | version of a publication / adding | A new edition. In addition to this. |
| **Complement** / **Compliment** | something that completes / praise | Rice complements dal. She paid me a compliment. |
| **Council** / **Counsel** | group of people / advice; a lawyer | Town council. Seek legal counsel. |
| **Moral** / **Morale** | lesson; ethical / confidence, spirit | The moral of the story. Team morale. |
| **Personal** / **Personnel** | private / staff | Personal matter. Army personnel. |
| **Principal** / **Principle** | head; main; capital sum / rule, belief | The school principal. A man of principle. |
| **Stationary** / **Stationery** | not moving / paper, pens | A stationary bus. Office stationery. |
| **Ordinance** / **Ordnance** | order, decree / military supplies | President's ordinance. Ordnance factory. |

lessons.title: Homophones: same sound, different spelling
lessons.body:
Some pairs below only sound *nearly* alike (draught /drɑːft/ vs drought /draʊt/; decent vs descent; desert, the dry region, vs dessert). They are kept here because exams test them together.

| Words | Meanings | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Altar** / **Alter** | holy table / change | Kneel at the altar. Alter the plan. |
| **Canvas** / **Canvass** | cloth / seek votes | A canvas bag. Canvass for votes. |
| **Capital** / **Capitol** | chief city, money / US Congress building | Shillong is the capital. The Capitol in Washington. |
| **Cite** / **Site** / **Sight** | quote / place / vision, view | Cite a case. Building site. Lose one's sight. |
| **Coarse** / **Course** | rough / path, programme of study | Coarse cloth. A degree course. |
| **Decent** / **Descent** / **Dissent** | proper / going down / disagreement | Decent clothes. A steep descent. Voice of dissent. |
| **Desert** / **Dessert** | dry region; to abandon / sweet dish | Thar desert. Ice cream for dessert. |
| **Hoard** / **Horde** | secret store / huge crowd | A hoard of gold. Hordes of tourists. |
| **Draught** / **Drought** | current of air / long period without rain | A cold draught. A severe drought. |
| **Canon** / **Cannon** | rule, law / big gun | Canons of good taste. Fire the cannon. |
| **Cereal** / **Serial** | grain food / in a series | Breakfast cereal. A TV serial. |
| **Peace** / **Piece** | calm / a part | World peace. A piece of cake. |
| **Pray** / **Prey** | worship / hunted animal | Pray daily. The tiger's prey. |
| **Role** / **Roll** | part played / list; to turn over | A leading role. Roll call. |
| **Stair** / **Stare** | step / look fixedly | Climb the stairs. Don't stare. |
| **Waist** / **Waste** | middle of the body / misuse | A 32-inch waist. Waste of time. |
| **Vain** / **Vane** / **Vein** | proud; useless / weather indicator / blood vessel | In vain. A weather vane. A blue vein. |
| **Bare** / **Bear** | naked, uncovered / animal; to tolerate | Bare feet. Bear the pain. |
| **Die** / **Dye** | stop living / colour | Plants die without water. Dye the cloth. |
| **Fair** / **Fare** | just; a mela / ticket price | A fair decision. Bus fare. |
| **Weather** / **Whether** | climate / if | Cold weather. Tell me whether you'll come. |
| **Principal** / **Principle** | (repeated here because it is the most-asked homophone) | The principal's principle is honesty. |
| **Brake** / **Break** | stopping device / to shatter; a pause | Apply the brake. A tea break. |
| **Sole** / **Soul** | only; bottom of the foot / spirit | Sole owner. Body and soul. |
| **Steal** / **Steel** | rob / metal | Steal a purse. Steel plant. |
| **Suite** / **Sweet** | set of rooms / sugary | Hotel suite. Sweet tea. |
| **Wholly** / **Holy** | completely / sacred | Wholly wrong. A holy place. |

lessons.title: Spelling rules that cover most exam words
lessons.body:
### 1. I before E, except after C (when the sound is "ee")
believe, achieve, relieve, field, siege | receive, ceiling, deceive, conceit.
**Exceptions to memorise:** seize, weird, either, neither, leisure, protein, species, caffeine. Also *ei* when it sounds "ay": neighbour, weigh, eight, reign.

### 2. Doubling the final consonant
- One syllable, one vowel + one consonant, then a vowel suffix: **double**. run → running, stop → stopped, sit → sitting.
- Two syllables with stress on the **last** syllable: **double**. be'gin → beginning, oc'cur → occurred, re'fer → referred, com'mit → committed, pre'fer → preferred.
- Stress on the **first** syllable: **don't double**. 'visit → visited, 'offer → offered, 'benefit → benefited, 'target → targeted.
- Stress moves away: re'fer → **'ref**erence (one r), pre'fer → **'pref**erence.
- British English doubles a final **l** anyway: travel → travelled, cancel → cancelled, label → labelled (American: traveled).

### 3. Silent final E
- Drop it before a vowel suffix: hope → hoping, write → writing, desire → desirable.
- Keep it before a consonant suffix: hope → hopeful, care → careful, move → movement.
- Keep it after soft c/g before a/o: notice**able**, manage**able**, change**able**, courage**ous**.
- Exceptions: argue → argument, true → truly, due → duly, whole → wholly, nine → ninth.

### 4. Final Y
- Consonant + y: change y to i. happy → happiness, carry → carried, beauty → beautiful.
- But keep y before -ing: carrying, studying, flying.
- Vowel + y: keep y. play → played, enjoy → enjoyment. (Exceptions: pay → paid, say → said, lay → laid, day → daily.)

### 5. Prefixes never change the root
dis + appear = **disappear** (one s), dis + satisfy = **dissatisfy** (two s), mis + spell = **misspell**, un + necessary = **unnecessary**, im + mature = **immature**, il + legal = **illegal**.

### 6. -ful, all-, and -cede/-ceed/-sede
- The suffix is **-ful** with one l: careful, hopeful, spoonful; and **fulfil** (British).
- *all* + word loses an l: already, almost, altogether, always. But **all right** is two words.
- Only **supersede** ends in -sede. Only **exceed, proceed, succeed** end in -ceed. Everything else is -cede: precede, recede, concede, accede, secede, intercede.

### 7. -able vs -ible (useful guide)
If the root is a complete word, usually **-able**: accept**able**, read**able**, comfort**able**, depend**able**. If the root is not a word by itself, usually **-ible**: vis**ible**, aud**ible**, ed**ible**, poss**ible**, terr**ible**.

### 8. Plurals
| Rule | Examples |
|---|---|
| s, sh, ch, x, z add -es | buses, bushes, churches, boxes |
| consonant + y → ies | city → cities, lady → ladies (but boy → boys) |
| f / fe → ves | knife → knives, leaf → leaves, wife, life, half, wolf, thief, shelf |
| …but just add -s | roofs, chiefs, beliefs, proofs, cliffs, safes |
| o → oes | potatoes, tomatoes, heroes, echoes, mosquitoes |
| o → os | photos, pianos, radios, kilos, zoos |
| Latin/Greek | criterion → criteria, phenomenon → phenomena, datum → data, medium → media, crisis → crises, analysis → analyses, thesis → theses |
| Irregular | child → children, ox → oxen, mouse → mice, tooth → teeth |
| Same form | sheep, deer, fish, series, species |
| Compound nouns: pluralise the main word | sisters-in-law, passers-by, commanders-in-chief |
| Always plural | scissors, trousers, spectacles |
| Never plural (uncountable) | information, furniture, luggage, advice, equipment, news |

> Indian exams follow **British spelling**: colour, centre, defence, programme, travelled, jewellery, manoeuvre.

lessons.title: Commonly misspelt words
lessons.body:
The trap letter is shown in capitals in the middle column.

| Correct | Where people go wrong | Memory tip |
|---|---|---|
| accommodate | aCCoMModate | two c's and two m's: room for everyone |
| achieve | achIEve | i before e |
| acquire | aCQuire | acquaint, acquit, acquire all have cq |
| address | aDDreSS | double d, double s |
| aggressive | aGGreSSive | double g, double s |
| amateur | amatEUR | ends like "chauffeur" (-eur) |
| apparent | aPParEnt | "a parent" is apparent |
| argument | argUment | argue drops its e |
| assassination | aSSaSSination | "ass + ass + ination" |
| beginning | begiNNing | stress on "gin" doubles n |
| believe | belIEve | never beLIEve a lie |
| bureaucracy | bUREAUcracy | bureau + cracy |
| business | bUSIness | "bus + i + ness" |
| calendar | calendAr | ends in -ar |
| category | catEgory | "cat" + "ego" + "ry" |
| cemetery | cemEtEry | three e's (people scream "e-e-e") |
| colleague | colLEAGUE | col + league |
| commitment | coMMiTment | double m, single t |
| committee | coMMiTTEE | double m, double t, double e |
| conscience | conSCIence | con + science |
| conscientious | conSCIENTious | conscience + tious |

| definitely | defINITEly | contains "finite" |
| dilemma | dileMMa | "Emma" has a dilemma |
| disappear | diSaPPear | dis + appear |

| gauge | gAUge | a before u |

| grammar | grammAr | -ar, not -er |

| harass | haRaSS | one r, two s |
| hierarchy | hIErarchy | "hi, er, archy" |

| independent | independEnt | ends -ent |
| indispensable | indispensAble | ends -able |
| intelligence | inteLLigence | double l |
| jewellery | jeweLLery | British: jewel + lery |

| misspell | miSSpell | mis + spell |
| necessary | neCeSSary | one collar (c), two sleeves (ss) |
| noticeable | noticEable | keep e after c |
| occasion | oCCaSion | double c, single s |
| occurred | oCCuRRed | double c, double r |
| occurrence | oCCuRRence | double c, double r, -ence |

examples.q:
Fill in the blanks: "The ___ of the school said that honesty is a ___ he never compromises on."
(a) principle, principal (b) principal, principle (c) principal, principal (d) principle, principle
examples.solution:
First blank = head of a school = principal (a person; "the principal is your PAL").
Second blank = a rule or belief = principle (principLE = ruLE).
Answer: (b) principal, principle

examples.q:
Fill in the blanks: "Heavy rain will ___ the harvest, and its ___ will be felt in prices."
(a) effect, affect (b) affect, affect (c) affect, effect (d) effect, effect
examples.solution:
First blank comes after "will", so it needs a verb: affect (to influence).
Second blank comes after "its", so it needs a noun: effect (result).
Answer: (c) affect, effect
examples.shortcut: A for Action (verb), E for End result (noun).

examples.q:
Choose the correctly spelt word.
(a) Accomodation (b) Acommodation (c) Accommodation (d) Accommadation
examples.solution:
Rule for this word: double c AND double m ("room for two c's and two m's").
(a) has one m, (b) one c, (d) wrong vowel.
Answer: (c) Accommodation

examples.q:
Which of these is spelt correctly?
(a) Occured (b) Occurred (c) Ocurred (d) Occurrd
examples.solution:
occur: stress on the last syllable (oc-CUR), ends in vowel + consonant.
Adding the vowel suffix -ed, so double the final r: occurred.
The c is double in the root itself (oc-cur).
Answer: (b) Occurred
examples.shortcut: Compare with "visited": stress on VIS-, so there is no doubling.

examples.q:
Identify the MISSPELT word.
(a) Receive (b) Seize (c) Wierd (d) Ceiling
examples.solution:
Receive and Ceiling follow "e before i after c".
Seize and Weird are famous exceptions: they are written with ei.
So "Wierd" is wrong; correct is Weird.
Answer: (c) Wierd

examples.q:
Fill in the blank: "There were ___ vehicles on the road during the bandh."
(a) less (b) fewer (c) lesser (d) little
examples.solution:
Vehicles can be counted, so use fewer.
Less is for uncountable nouns (less traffic, less water).
Lesser means "smaller in importance" (a lesser evil); little also goes with uncountable nouns.
Answer: (b) fewer

traps: Affect vs Effect has two rare uses that exam-setters love: "effect" as a verb means to bring about ("The CEO effected a change"), and "affect" as a noun (emotion) appears only in psychology. For fill-in questions, first decide verb or noun.
Its vs It's: "it's" ALWAYS equals "it is/it has". If you cannot expand it to "it is", write "its". The same test works for who's/whose, you're/your, they're/their.
Stationary vs Stationery: stationEry has E for Envelopes; stationAry has A for "At rest".
Complement vs Compliment: complEment complEtes something; complIment is praise that "I" like to receive.
Dropping one of a double letter is the most common spelling error: accommodate, embarrass, committee, occurrence, millennium, questionnaire. Check each doubled consonant separately.
Principal vs Principle: principal is a person or "main/chief" (the principal reason) or a sum of money; principle is always a rule or belief.

practice.q: Fill in the blank: The ____ of the college gave away the prizes on Founders' Day.
practice.explanation: Principal = head of an institution (a person). Principle = a rule or belief. Hook: the principal is your PAL.

practice.q: Fill in the blank: Please order some ____ for the office: pens, files and envelopes.
practice.explanation: Stationery = writing materials. Stationary = not moving. Hook: stationEry has E for Envelopes.

practice.q: Fill in the blank: After three straight wins, the ____ of the team was very high.
practice.explanation: Morale = confidence and spirit of a group. Moral = a lesson or ethical principle. Hook: morALE has the extra E for Energy.

practice.q: Fill in the blank: Her ____ design for collecting rainwater on the hillside won a state award.
practice.explanation: Ingenious = clever and inventive (adjective, fits before "design"). Ingenuous = innocent/naive; Indigenous = native; Ingenuity is a noun. Hook: ingenIous has the I of Intelligence, ingenUous has the U of Unsuspecting.

practice.q: Fill in the blank: The doctor will ____ you to take complete rest for a week.
practice.explanation: "will ___ you" needs a verb: advise. Advice is the noun (take my advice). Hook: the verb has S as in "Suggest".

practice.q: Fill in the blank: Dark clouds have gathered; a thunderstorm is ____.
practice.explanation: Imminent = about to happen. Eminent = famous and respected; Immanent = present within; Imminence is a noun. Hook: IMMinent = IMMediately coming.

practice.q: Fill in the blank: The childless couple decided to ____ a baby girl from the orphanage.
practice.explanation: Adopt = take as one's own. Adapt = adjust; Adept = skilled; Adoption is a noun and cannot follow "to". Hook: adOpt means Own it; adApt means Adjust.

practice.q: Fill in the blank: Migrants from the plains take time to ____ to the cold climate of the hills.
practice.explanation: Adapt = adjust to new conditions. Adaptable is an adjective and cannot follow "to" here. Hook: adApt means Adjust, adOpt means Own.

practice.q: Fill in the blank: The ____ villager believed every rumour he heard at the market.
practice.explanation: Credulous = too ready to believe. Credible = believable (a credible story); Creditable = praiseworthy; Credential = a qualification. Hook: credULOUS people are gULLible.

practice.q: Fill in the blank: This year there were ____ applicants for the post than last year.
practice.explanation: Applicants are countable, so use fewer. Less is for uncountable nouns (less money). Hook: FEWer for things you can count on your FINGERS.

practice.q: Fill in the blank: The state decided to ____ the officer for accepting bribes.
practice.explanation: Prosecute = take legal action against. Persecute = harass or oppress (usually for belief or identity); Proscribe = ban; Prescribe = recommend. Hook: PROsecute = the PROsecutor goes to court.

practice.q: Fill in the blank: Please be ____ about this matter and do not discuss it with anyone.
practice.explanation: Discreet = careful, tactful in what one says. Discrete = separate, distinct (discrete parts). Discretion is a noun. Hook: in discrETE the two e's are kept apart by the t, so it means separate.

practice.q: Fill in the blank: The two neighbouring states reached an ____ settlement of their boundary dispute.
practice.explanation: Amicable describes friendly relations, agreements and settlements; Amiable describes a person's nature. Amenable = willing to be persuaded; Ambivalent = having mixed feelings. Hook: amiCABLE is for a CABLE between two parties (an agreement).

practice.q: Fill in the blank: 21 January 1972, when Meghalaya became a full-fledged state, was a ____ day for its people.
practice.explanation: Historic = important, famous in history (a historic day, a historic victory). Historical = relating to history (historical records, a historical novel). Hook: historIC = Important Coming-of-age moment.

practice.q: Fill in the blank: He is ____ to taking any risk with public money.
practice.explanation: Averse (to) = strongly unwilling, opposed. Adverse = unfavourable (adverse weather). Aversion is a noun. Hook: AVERSE people have an AVERSION; ADVERSE conditions are ADVERSaries.

practice.q: Fill in the blank: ____ going to the Shillong Cherry Blossom Festival next week.
practice.explanation: They're = they are. Test: "They are going" makes sense. Their = belonging to them; There = that place. Hook: if you can expand it, use the apostrophe.

practice.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
practice.explanation: accommodate has double c AND double m. Hook: it is big enough to accommodate two c's and two m's.

practice.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
practice.explanation: embarrass has double r and double s. Hook: Really Red, So Shy.

practice.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
practice.explanation: occur + ence: the r doubles (stress on "-cur") and the ending is -ence. Hook: double c, double r, then -ence.

practice.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
practice.explanation: separate has "a" after p. Hook: there is "a rat" in sep-A-RAT-e.

practice.q: Choose the MISSPELT word.
practice.explanation: The rule is i before e except after c. Believe has no c before the vowels, so it takes ie: believe. Receive and Ceiling take ei after c; Achieve takes ie. Hook: never beLIEve a LIE.

practice.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
practice.explanation: conscientious = conscience + -tious (the c of conscience becomes t). It keeps "sci" and the i before -ous. Hook: CON-SCIENT-IOUS; a conscientious student works with SCIENcE.

practice.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
practice.explanation: mischief + -ous = mischievous (three syllables: MIS-chi-vous). There is no "i" after v. Hook: pronounce it right and you spell it right; there is no "-vious".

practice.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
practice.explanation: questionnaire has double n and ends in -aire (a French ending, as in millionaire). Hook: a questionnaire asks Numerous Numbers of questions, hence nn.

practice.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
practice.explanation: privilege: there is no d, and the vowels are i-i-e-e. Hook: it is a privilege to have no "edge" (no d) in it.

practice.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
practice.explanation: entrepreneur is French: entre + pre + neur. It is not "enter". Hook: ENTRE-PRE-NEUR, with the same -eur ending as amateur and chauffeur.

practice.q: Fill in the correctly spelt word: The matter was ____ to a higher authority.
practice.explanation: re-FER is stressed on the last syllable, so the final r doubles before -ed: referred. But REF-erence has one r because the stress moves. Hook: stress on the end, double the end.

practice.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
practice.explanation: notice + able keeps the e so that c stays soft ("s" sound). The same happens in manageable and changeable. Hook: the E keeps the C Soft.

practice.q: Choose the correct plural form.
practice.explanation: In compound nouns, pluralise the main noun only: sisters-in-law, passers-by, commanders-in-chief. Hook: pluralise the PERSON, not the law.

practice.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
practice.explanation: Supersede is the ONLY English word ending in -sede. Only exceed, proceed and succeed take -ceed; everything else takes -cede (precede, concede). Some dictionaries note "supercede" as a variant, but the exam-standard spelling is supersede. Hook: super + SEDEre (Latin "to sit"), so it sits above.
